title: Neuromorphic chips
summary: Spiking neurons that work only when something happens. Tune one to spot a pattern.

ideas.how: many simple neurons, each with its own memory
neurons spend energy only when a spike arrives

measures.how: spikes do work only when something happens

then: Neural networks are mostly theory; neuromorphic engineering begins in the late 1980s.
Research chips copy neurons and synapses in silicon.
Big spiking chips appear: IBM TrueNorth (2014) and Intel Loihi (2017).
Systems reach a billion neurons, and neuromorphic microcontrollers ship for sensors.
Projection: spiking chips in always-on sensors and robots; large-scale use still unproven.

challenges.title: Spot the pattern
challenges.task: Tune a spiking neuron to fire for pattern A and never for noise.

ask: How is a spiking neuron different from a neural-network neuron?
What are neuromorphic chips good at today?
Can neuromorphic chips run large language models?
